pairs.subject: admission-queue
pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/shed.rs:186 A timeout releases the HTTP-held permit while blocking store work can continue, allowing subsequent requests to increase backend occupancy beyond the configured cap.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/shed.rs:207 Capacity refusal returns a stable overloaded code with HTTP 503, distinct from budget refusal and internal failure, and is counted.

crates/api/src/otlp/semconv.rs:216 Inherited resource-level prompts become owned payloads on every mapped span without an aggregate expanded-size budget; mapping also precedes the native batch-count check.
crates/api/src/shed.rs:133 The gate reads its own semaphore availability rather than platform-free capacity; there is no platform-free denominator requiring a reserved-cache correction.
crates/api/src/shed.rs:82 Numeric zero disables the bound, contrary to the technique's prohibition on magic unlimited values; timed-out blocking jobs can also outlive their permits.
crates/api/src/shed.rs:173 Admission checks permit availability without consulting host or container pressure; no pressure thresholds, hysteresis, or probe-failure posture were found.

crates/api/src/shed.rs:172 Every origin competes for the entire global permit budget without per-origin occupancy limits, so one tenant can occupy every slot; spend caps do not bound concurrent occupancy.
crates/api/src/shed.rs:169 Single-event, batch, and OTLP routes share this process guard for the selected store backend; ingress capacity is not partitioned into independent per-route pools.

crates/api/src/shed.rs:216 These are stateless, replay-safe telemetry submissions with reasoned refusal and a retry hint; no expensive long-lived caller establishment was found to justify holding callers.

crates/api/src/shed.rs:79 The concurrency ceiling is resolved independently of body-size ceilings and the shipped 512Mi container memory limit; no evaluated derivation preserves headroom below destructive memory enforcement.
crates/api/src/shed.rs:60 Tiny events and multi-megabyte batches each consume one permit; separate per-request byte caps provide neither aggregate byte accounting nor a host-derived occupancy budget.
crates/api/src/events_batch.rs:200 These paths persist explicitly submitted telemetry; searches found no prefetch, speculative submission, or redundant execution fan-out.

crates/api/src/shed.rs:248 The ingest surface reports outstanding HTTP permits without separating backend waiting from execution or exposing oldest wait; continuing blocking jobs disappear from this gauge after HTTP timeout.

crates/api/src/access_layer.rs:166 Authentication precedes the nonblocking ingest gate and performs blocking-pool store lookups, so a full gate's refusal can wait behind backend work or become an authentication timeout.
